react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent enrichment paradigms converge on a single dominant biological signal: perturbation of Galactose Metabolism (KEGG:map00052 / KEGG:hsa00052). RaMP multi-DB ORA returned this pathway at rank 2 with FDR 8.76×10⁻¹⁵ and a fold enrichment of 1452, driven by five input metabolites — myo-inositol, sucrose, galactitol, glycerol, and galactinol — that constitute over one-sixth of the pathway's entire compound roster. Mummichog's m/z-direct network analysis independently recovered the same pathway (p=0.00891, rank 4) with a 91.7% overlap (11 of 12 pathway members hit), demonstrating that mass-coincidence and ID-based ORA reach the same biological conclusion from different feature spaces. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA confirmed the finding at p=5.65×10⁻⁹ (rank 1) with the same five compound hits. The Galactosemia disease map (SMPDB:SMP00182) achieved the lowest FDR in the RaMP result (8.76×10⁻¹⁵), reflecting the direct pathological relevance of this metabolite cluster. Aspirin (acetylsalicylate) independently enriched in Transport of small molecules (FDR 5.39×10⁻⁵) and the WikiPathways Aspirin and miRNAs pathway (FDR 7.85×10⁻⁴), consistent with its known COX-independent metabolic effects. Glycerol additionally appeared in glycerophospholipid metabolism pathways as a structural phospholipid precursor. The biological story is one of systemic carbohydrate flux disruption: the five galactose-family metabolites form a tight co-abundance cluster that reflects a perturbation in the Leloir pathway, potentially consistent with galactosemia or an intervention that impairs galactose-to-glucose interconversion.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent enrichment paradigms converge on Galactose Metabolism (KEGG:map00052 / SMPDB:SMP00043) as the dominant biological signal. RaMP ORA returned this pathway at rank 1 with FDR 8.76e-15, with five input metabolites mapping to its roster: sucrose, myo-inositol, galactitol, galactinol, and glycerol. Mummichog confirmed the same pathway at rank 3 with p-value 7.65e-3, using m/z and network proximity rather than ID annotation. Glycerol and myo-inositol additionally populated the Glycerophospholipid biosynthetic pathway (WP:WP2533, FDR 2.02e-4) and the Transport of small molecules Reactome super-pathway (R-HSA-382551, FDR 5.39e-5). Aspirin mapped to Transport of small molecules via acetylsalicylate, reflecting its known small-molecule transport pharmacology. Methionine sulfoxide and allysine did not achieve significance in any single pathway but contribute co-abundance context. The convergence of ORA and network-diffusion on Galactose Metabolism, with five shared driver metabolites across methods, constitutes a high-confidence biological finding.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent enrichment methods converge on Galactose Metabolism as the dominant biological signal in the treatment-group metabolome. The RaMP multi-database ORA assigns FDR 8.76e-15 to both the Galactosemia (SMPDB:SMP00182) and Galactose Metabolism (SMPDB:SMP00043, KEGG:map00052) pathways, with five shared driver metabolites detected across both: myo-inositol (KEGG:C00137), sucrose (KEGG:C00089), galactitol (KEGG:C01697), glycerol (KEGG:C00116), and galactinol (KEGG:C01235). MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently confirms Galactose Metabolism (KEGG:hsa00052) as the top hit with p = 5.65e-09. Mummichog m/z-direct analysis corroborates this finding, ranking Galactose metabolism (MUMM:galactose_metabolism) at rank 3 with near-complete pathway overlap. In the m/z-driven network, myo-inositol, D-glucose, sucrose, galactitol, and galactinol additionally populate Sialic acid metabolism (MUMM:sialic_acid_metabolism) and Hexose phosphorylation (MUMM:hexose_phosphorylation). Glycerol and myo-inositol also appear in the Glycerophospholipid biosynthetic pathway (WP:WP2533) per RaMP ORA (FDR 2.02e-04, rank 7) and Glycerophospholipid metabolism (MUMM:glycerophospholipid_metabolism) per mummichog. Aspirin (KEGG:C01405) maps to the Reactome Transport of small molecules super-pathway (REACT:R-HSA-382551, FDR 5.39e-05, rank 3) via its metabolite acetylsalicylate. Methionine sulfoxide (KEGG:C02989) and allysine (KEGG:C04076) do not achieve significance in any single pathway at the FDR 0.05 threshold but may contribute peripheral contextual signal.

use run_ramp_enrichment (multi-DB ORA, broader namespace coverage) or run_metaboanalystr_psea (KEGG-specific ORA) instead

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent enrichment paradigms converge on a single dominant biological signal: perturbation of Galactose Metabolism (KEGG:map00052 / KEGG:hsa00052). RaMP multi-DB ORA returned this pathway at rank 2 with FDR 8.76×10⁻¹⁵ and a fold enrichment of 1452, driven by five input metabolites — myo-inositol, sucrose, galactitol, glycerol, and galactinol — that constitute over one-sixth of the pathway's entire compound roster. Mummichog's m/z-direct network analysis independently recovered the same pathway (p=0.00891, rank 4) with a 91.7% overlap (11 of 12 pathway members hit), demonstrating that mass-coincidence and ID-based ORA reach the same biological conclusion from different feature spaces. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA confirmed the finding at p=5.65×10⁻⁹ (rank 1) with the same five compound hits. The Galactosemia disease map (SMPDB:SMP00182) achieved the lowest FDR in the RaMP result (8.76×10⁻¹⁵), reflecting the direct pathological relevance of this metabolite cluster. Aspirin (acetylsalicylate) independently enriched in Transport of small molecules (FDR 5.39×10⁻⁵) and the WikiPathways Aspirin and miRNAs pathway (FDR 7.85×10⁻⁴), consistent with its known COX-independent metabolic effects. Glycerol additionally appeared in glycerophospholipid metabolism pathways as a structural phospholipid precursor. The biological story is one of systemic carbohydrate flux disruption: the five galactose-family metabolites form a tight co-abundance cluster that reflects a perturbation in the Leloir pathway, potentially consistent with galactosemia or an intervention that impairs galactose-to-glucose interconversion.
